---
title: "A visual tour"
description: >
  Every verb in tidycjk, shown on real CJK text rather than described.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(tidycjk)
```

Each figure below was drawn by `data-raw/make-figures.R` using the package
itself — the terminal grids are laid out by `cjk_width()`, so they cannot
drift from what the functions actually return.

## Width is not character count

<img src="../reference/figures/hero-width.svg" width="100%" alt="Padding by character count leaves a CJK column ragged; padding by display width aligns it." />

`nchar()` counts characters. A terminal counts columns, and a CJK character
takes two of them. That single mismatch is why CJK tables print ragged.

```{r width}
labels <- c("中文", "abcd", "日本語")

nchar(labels)
cjk_width(labels)

cat(paste0("|", cjk_pad(labels, 8), "|"), sep = "\n")
```

Truncation follows the same rule — a cut at eight columns, not eight
characters:

```{r truncate}
cjk_truncate("我今天很開心", 8)
```

## Which script, which language

<img src="../reference/figures/fig-scripts.png" width="100%" alt="cjk_script and cjk_detect_language over five sample strings." />

```{r script}
txt <- c("我今天很開心", "こんにちは", "안녕하세요", "東京都", "no CJK here")

cjk_script(txt)
cjk_detect_language(txt)
```

Rows one and four come back `NA`. Both are written entirely in Han
characters, and nothing in the script separates Japanese from Chinese there.
A library that answers `"chinese"` is guessing, and it will be wrong on
Japanese input in a way you cannot detect downstream. Opt in if you want it:

```{r script-optin}
cjk_detect_language(txt, han_only = "chinese")
```

## How much of it is CJK

<img src="../reference/figures/fig-ratio.png" width="100%" alt="cjk_ratio over four sample strings, shown as filled bars." />

```{r ratio}
cjk_ratio(c("我今天很開心", "hello 中文 world", "東京都 2024", "no CJK here"))
```

The denominator is every code point, spaces and Latin punctuation included.
At the column level:

```{r summary}
posts <- data.frame(id = 1:5, text = txt)

cjk_summary(posts, text)
cjk_char_counts(posts, text)
```

## Segmentation

<img src="../reference/figures/fig-tokens.png" width="100%" alt="cjk_segment splitting a mixed string into tokens." />

```{r segment}
cjk_segment("hello 中文 world", engine = "character")

cjk_tokens(posts[1:2, ], text, engine = "character")
```

`engine` is required. Where a word ends is a fact about a language rather
than about Unicode, so no dictionary is bundled, and quietly handing back
character tokens to someone who asked for words is the mistake this package
exists to avoid.

```{r engines}
cjk_segmenters()
```

## Width forms

<img src="../reference/figures/fig-normalize.png" width="100%" alt="to_halfwidth narrows width forms and leaves everything else alone." />

```{r halfwidth}
to_halfwidth("１２３")
as.numeric(to_halfwidth("１２３"))

# NFKC would rewrite all three of these; to_halfwidth leaves them alone
to_halfwidth("½ Ⅸ ①")

# halfwidth katakana: two code points composed into one
x <- "ｶﾞ"
nchar(x)
nchar(to_halfwidth(x))
to_halfwidth(x) == "ガ"
```

<img src="../reference/figures/fig-blocks.png" width="100%" alt="The first rows of the cjk_blocks table." />

head(cjk_blocks(), 10)
